theme: Airbnb host-side datasets: superhost/multi-listing/professional host panels, host earnings, DAC7 platform-reporting statistics, IRS/tax authority STR income stats
queries_run: gh search repos "airbnb host income" --sort updated
gh search repos "multi-listing host" OR "professional host" airbnb --sort updated
gh search repos "commercial host" airbnb multi listing --sort updated (0 results)
gh search repos "1099-K short-term rental" OR "STR income tax" --sort updated (near-empty)
gh search repos "hostaway" OR "guesty" api export earnings --sort updated
WebFetch raw READMEs for FabianRoger/AirDNA_Size_Fractions and awpape/NYC-Airbnb-Commercial-Host-Scoring- to check relevance

candidates.name: dac7-validator
candidates.what_it_holds: TypeScript validator/CLI for OECD DPI / EU DAC7 XML platform-reporting schemas (the XSD structure platforms like Airbnb use to file seller income/nights data with EU tax authorities). No aggregate statistics or actual filings, but documents the exact fields (gross amount paid, number of transactions, property nights, address) that DAC7 filings must contain -- useful as a schema reference if we ever chase national tax-authority aggregate DAC7 publications.
candidates.why_useful: Gap 12 (EU DAC7 platform reporting statistics): shows what fields exist in the underlying filings even though no repo here holds published aggregates.
candidates.size_hint: small code repo, no data files

candidates.name: dac7_reporter
candidates.what_it_holds: Application to submit signed DAC7 report files to a national DIP (Digital Platform) API. Compliance tooling for platforms filing seller/host income reports, not a statistics dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Same schema-reference value as dac7-validator; confirms DAC7 filings carry host-level gross-income and nights fields that in aggregate (if a tax authority ever publishes summary stats) would proxy host earnings.
candidates.size_hint: small code repo, no data files

candidates.name: dac7
candidates.what_it_holds: Tools to build and validate DAC7 declarations (Python library, from an e-commerce marketplace company, generalized for any platform operator including short-term rental platforms).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: confirms the DAC7 declaration format and required host/seller fields; no actual Airbnb or STR data.

candidates.name: dac7-dpi-client-php
candidates.what_it_holds: PHP client for the Polish DAC7 DPI API, letting a platform operator submit seller/host reports (DPI-FR registration, DPI-IS seller reports) to the Polish tax administration (KAS).
candidates.why_useful: Points to a specific national API (Poland) where, in principle, aggregate/statistical releases about DAC7-reported platform income could originate; no data itself.

candidates.name: Airbnb-superhosts-crawler-with-data-analyzer
candidates.what_it_holds: A 2018 crawler + analyzer targeting Airbnb superhost profile pages to study superhost behavior patterns (not committed as a bulk dataset; it is a scraper of airbnb.com, which our rules mark as a method to catalogue and NOT run).
candidates.why_useful: Only concrete GitHub method found aimed specifically at superhost-status data collection off Airbnb itself; illustrates the shape of a possible future scrape target (superhost badges/portfolio pages) but is stale (2018) and would need a human ToS decision to ever run.
candidates.size_hint: small scraper + analyzer scripts, unclear if any sample data is committed

candidates.name: airdna
candidates.what_it_holds: An independent third-party API profile/documentation of AirDNA's Enterprise API surface (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates) -- not the data itself, and AirDNA is a paid/licensed vendor, but the repo documents exactly which host/property-level metrics (occupancy, ADR, revenue estimates) are exposed if the team ever licenses AirDNA.
candidates.why_useful: Gap 2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs) -- confirms AirDNA's API shape as a reference even though access itself is paid.

notes: This theme came back very sparse on GitHub. Extensive keyword variants for 'superhost dataset', 'multi-listing host', 'professional host', 'host income', 'host earnings', '1099-K short-term rental', 'STR income tax', DAC7, and property-management-platform (Hostaway/Guesty) API exports produced almost nothing but: (a) generic ML-classroom notebooks that re-derive host_is_superhost from the well-known Kaggle NYC-2019 / Inside-Airbnb-derived files (excluded per rules -- e.g. bjalloh910/Airbnb_Superhost_Prediction_Model, ATadmuri-hub/Airbnb-Superhost-Price-Prediction, Laeeq14/..., suhanagupta08/..., and ~20 more of the same shape, none included above), (b) unrelated hardware/DAC-chip repos that collide on the 'DAC7' string (TI/Adafruit/STM32 digital-to-analog-converter parts -- excluded), and (c) DAC7 COMPLIANCE tooling (schema validators, filing-submission clients) built for platforms to FILE reports, not published aggregate statistics from any tax authority about what platforms reported. I found no repo anywhere holding an actual superhost panel, a multi-listing/portfolio-size time series, host earnings data, or any national tax authority's aggregate DAC7/STR-income statistics release. The genuinely closest thing to a 'commercial host scoring' dataset (awpape/NYC-Airbnb-Commercial-Host-Scoring-) is explicitly built on the single well-known Kaggle AB_NYC_2019.csv file and is excluded per the exclusion rule, though its methodology (5-signal composite: availability, review frequency, minimum-nights, portfolio size, pricing) could be a design reference if the team ever revisits our own Inside Airbnb 13-city panel to derive a synthetic 'professional host share' proxy from listing-level patterns instead of looking for one pre-built externally. Overall verdict: IRS/tax-authority STR income statistics and DAC7 aggregate reporting statistics do not appear to exist as open, committed GitHub datasets -- if these are wanted, the path is likely direct national statistical-office or tax-authority publications (e.g. Eurostat, member-state DAC7 transparency reports), not GitHub, and that lookup would need a non-GitHub (web) scout.
